Job Description

Group Lead, AI Governance at a glance..
Location : Toronto, ON
Hybrid : 3 days/week

The Kraft Heinz Information Technology organization is hiring a Group Lead, AI Governance to establish and operate the technical governance, platform controls and support model that enable safe, responsible and scalable use of AI across the enterprise. Based in Toronto, this leader will connect policy to day-to-day engineering practice across enterprise productivity AI, low-code agents and production-grade AI/ML solutions.

This is a hands-on leadership role (approximately 60% execution and 40% strategy). You will own the control framework and operating routines for platforms such as Microsoft 365 Copilot, Claude Enterprise, Microsoft Copilot Studio, Azure AI services and engineering patterns built with frameworks and observability tools such as LangGraph and LangSmith. You will partner with AI engineering, MLOps, security, legal, privacy, enterprise architecture, product and business teams to make risk-based decisions, remove delivery friction and ensure controls remain effective throughout the AI lifecycle.

What's on the menu?
- Lead the technical AI governance and platform support function, setting priorities, service expectations, operating routines and clear accountability across enterprise AI tools and custom AI solutions.
- Translate AI policies, risk appetite and regulatory obligations into practical engineering standards, approval criteria, platform configurations, reusable controls and evidence requirements.
- Own risk-tiered lifecycle governance from intake and experimentation through production approval, change management, monitoring, incident response and retirement, with proportionate checkpoints based on use-case criticality.
- Establish and maintain an enterprise inventory of AI tools, models, agents, use cases, owners, data dependencies, risk classifications, approvals and material changes.
- Support relevant teams on technical controls for identity and access, least privilege, data protection, secrets management, environment separation, vendor integrations, human oversight, logging, traceability and audit evidence.
- Set standards for AI evaluation and production readiness, including quality, safety, reliability, security, privacy, latency, cost and business acceptance criteria; ensure exceptions are documented, time-bound and remediated.
- Build observability and governance patterns for agentic systems, including prompt and response tracing, tool-call visibility, evaluation datasets, failure analysis, escalation paths and controls for autonomous actions.
- Govern and support AI platforms including Microsoft 365 Copilot, Claude Enterprise, Copilot Studio, Azure-based AI services and custom solutions using LangGraph, LangSmith and related MLOps/LLMOps capabilities.
- Lead AI platform intake, access and support processes; triage incidents and control gaps, coordinate root-cause analysis, track corrective actions and communicate material risks to the appropriate governance bodies.
- Partner with Legal, Privacy, Cybersecurity, Procurement, Internal Audit, Data Governance, Enterprise Architecture and business owners on use-case reviews, third-party assessments, control testing and audit readiness.
- Define governance metrics and service health indicators covering inventory completeness, review cycle time, control compliance, incidents, exceptions, evaluation coverage, adoption, consumption and remediation progress.
- Lead cross-functional initiatives and technical projects, managing scope, milestones, dependencies, decisions and stakeholder communications while coaching engineers and analysts on responsible AI practices.
- Monitor developments in AI regulation, standards, platform capabilities and emerging risks; assess their relevance and drive updates to controls, playbooks and technical roadmaps.

Recipe for success – apply now if this sounds like you!
- Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Data Science, Information Technology, Cybersecurity, or related field (advanced degree an asset)
- 7+ years of experience across MLOps, machine learning engineering, data science, cloud engineering, platform engineering, technology risk, or related disciplines, including responsibility for production AI/ML systems
- Hands-on experience designing, deploying, operating, or governing AI/ML platforms in a large, matrixed enterprise environment
- Practical understanding of AI risk management and responsible AI principles (accountability, transparency, privacy, security, reliability, safety, fairness, human oversight)
- Experience with cloud and identity controls, CI/CD, model/agent lifecycle management, observability, incident management, and production support (preferably Microsoft Azure)
- Experience with generative AI and agentic patterns (LLM applications, RAG, prompt/context engineering, tool use, agent workflows, evaluations, guardrails)
- Working knowledge of Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Studio; familiarity with Claude Enterprise, LangGraph, LangSmith, or comparable AI development/observability platforms strongly preferred
- Demonstrated technical project/program management experience (driving cross-functional work, managing dependencies, translating ambiguous requirements into executable plans)
- Strong written and verbal communication skills; able to explain technical risk, control design, and trade-offs to engineers, control functions, and senior business stakeholders
- Experience leading people, vendors, or matrixed delivery teams; developing practical standards that improve safety and delivery velocity
- Enterprise AI governance expertise (operating models, control frameworks, risk tiering, exception management, assurance, evidence-based decision making)
- MLOps and LLMOps expertise across development, deployment, monitoring, evaluation, change control, support, and retirement
- AI platform governance experience for employee productivity tools, low-code agents, third-party AI services, and custom production applications
- Knowledge of agentic AI risks and controls (permissions, tool access, prompt injection, data leakage, autonomous actions, human approval points, end-to-end traceability)
- Knowledge of data privacy, cybersecurity, model risk, third-party risk, intellectual property, regulatory compliance, AI FinOps, and business continuity considerations
- Pragmatic risk leadership style that preserves strong controls without unnecessary friction for delivery teams
- Comfort moving between executive-level governance discussions and detailed technical reviews with engineers and platform teams
- Structured operator mindset (clear ownership, repeatable processes, measurable service levels, disciplined follow-through)

The Senior Compensation Manager – Europe Developed Markets lies within the EPDM Region . You’ll be working in a high performing team and alongside HR and business stakeholders to deliver compensation programs that support our reward philosophy, attract and retain talent, and ensure market competitiveness across the region. You’ll be reporting into the Head of Rewards, EPDM. You will play a key role in ensuring EPDM adheres to the global compensation strategy, while owning the annual compensation routines across the Zone.

In brief, you are responsible for:

- Translating the global compensation strategy into the EPDM Zone and setting the Zone Compensation priorities
- Managing the annual merit cycle across the EPDM zone
- Partner with HR and business stakeholders to advise on compensation solutions for business challenges
- Determine and manage compensation projects within the EPDM Zone
- Responsible for ensuring the business is sized appropriately, using Korn Ferry Hay methodology, and supporting HR stakeholders in any org design
- Responsible for tools and analyses to enable employees to be paid fairly, competitively with the market and in alignment with our global compensation strategy
- Responsible for compensation documentation, toolkits and manager material for the EPDM Zone
- Ensure our HR leaders and business is aware of key compensation knowledge
- Manage the relationship with Global Compensation teams, and be the point person for Zone input on Global projects
- Responsible for managing the compensation governance for the Zone, ensuring alignment to global standards
- Lead, coach and develop the zone compensation team

Qualifications

- Strong experience in compensation and/or total rewards
- Experience using Korn Ferry Hay job evaluation methodology (or similar job architecture framework)
- Experience in salary benchmarking and compensation analyses
- Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret compensation data and provide actionable recommendations
- Prior people manager experience is a benefit

About Us

The Kraft Heinz Company is one of the largest food and beverage companies in the world, with eight   $1 billion + brands and global sales of approximately   $25 billion .   We’re   a globally trusted producer of high-quality, great-tasting, and nutritious foods for over 150 years. Our brands are truly global, with products produced and marketed in over 40 countries. These beloved products include condiments and sauces, cheese and dairy, meals, meats, refreshment beverages, coffee, infant and nutrition products, and   numerous   other grocery products in a portfolio of more than 200 legacy and emerging brands.

No matter the brand,   we’re   united under one vision:  To sustainably grow by delighting more consumers globally . Bringing this vision to life is our team of 39,000+ food lovers, creative thinkers, and high performers worldwide. Together, we help provide meals to those in need through our global partnership with Rise Against Hunger. We also stand committed to responsible, sustainable practices that extend to every   facet   of our business, our consumers, and our communities. Every day,   we’re   transforming the food industry with bold thinking and unprecedented results. If you share our passion – and are ready to create the future, build a legacy, and lead as a global citizen –   there’s   only one thing to do: join our table and   let’s   make life delicious!

Our Culture of Ownership, Meritocracy & Collaboration

We're   not afraid to think differently. Embrace   new ideas . Dream big. We empower our people at every level – from entry-level intern to senior   leader   – to own their work. We share a responsibility to think like Owners – to be mindful of the collective and sustained success of Kraft Heinz – which we apply to every situation, every day. As part of Kraft Heinz,   you're   supported to grow and achieve.   You’re   expected to bring your authentic self to work every day, to lead with humility, and drive outstanding performance at every level – and   you’ll   be rewarded.   You’re   given opportunities to leave a mark and build a legacy. Senior Analyst, Procurement Finance Intelligence at a glance...
You will be the hands-on builder supporting the Procurement Finance Intelligence capability at Kraft Heinz. Reporting directly to the Sr Manager Logistics Finance Intelligence, you will build and maintain the pipelines, dashboards, and AI agents that automate direct spend analytics — commodities, raw materials, and packaging. This is not a reporting analyst role. You write code, build pipelines, and ship tools that replace manual work. You are based in our Mexico Global Capability Center and are a core member of the Supply Chain Finance Intelligence team.
What’s on the menu?
- Build and maintain Snowflake data pipelines ingesting SAP/S4 procurement and direct spend data — ensuring clean, traceable, audit-ready inputs for all downstream analytics and agents

- Develop and maintain dashboards and automated reports covering direct spend analytics — price variance, coverage ratios, exposure concentration, and mark-to-market visibility

- Support the build and testing of Snowflake Cortex AI agents for procurement workflows — month-end close automation, forecast pack generation, and ad-hoc procurement finance requests

- Automate month-end close and forecast deliverables for Procurement Finance — replacing manual Excel processes with scheduled, validated, pipeline-driven outputs

- Support commodity hedge visibility reporting — build and maintain the data layer that feeds coverage ratio, open position, and threshold alert outputs for BU CFOs and Procurement leadership

- Perform data validation, reconciliation, and root-cause analysis when pipeline outputs don’t match expectations — you own the quality of what you build

- Document data models, pipeline logic, and agent prompts to the standard required by internal audit and the Finance AI Architecture team

- Collaborate closely with the Procurement Finance Intelligence Lead and peer analysts across the Supply Chain Finance Intelligence pillar to share patterns and avoid duplicating work

- I have 2–5 years of experience in finance, data analytics, or data engineering — with exposure to procurement, supply chain, or commodity finance preferred

- I understand basic procurement finance mechanics — price variance, coverage ratios, commodity exposure — well enough to validate that my outputs make sense

Job Description
The Kraft Heinz MBA Internship Program
The Kraft Heinz MBA Intern Program is designed to grow the future leaders of Kraft Heinz. This program is for high-performing, ambitious, and creative individuals who are ready to lead the future of food and beverage. Throughout the program, MBAs will hone their understanding of our business and industry, collaborate across the business to grow our iconic brands, and learn how to build their own legacy here at Kraft Heinz.

What’s On the Menu for the 2027 MBA Internship Program?
The Kraft Heinz MBA Internship Program is a ten-week experience at our Chicago headquarters during which interns will fully own a project end-to-end, enhance key leadership skills, and add value to critical efforts rooted in our Company’s growth plan. The ten-week program includes:
- One week of immersive onboarding to learn about our business and prepare important skills for a successful summer project

- Eight weeks dedicated to an impactful business project to explore new opportunities and unlock creative solutions

- One week of final presentations and closing reflections with our senior leadership

jobs.title: Sr. Manager, Procurement Risk & Resilience
jobs.location: Chicago/Aon Center, Illinois, United States of America
jobs.description:
Job Purpose

The Senior Manager, Procurement Risk & Resilience leads the North America Procurement risk management and resilience strategy and owns responsible sourcing compliance for the region. This role owns the frameworks, governance, tools and cross-functional routines used to identify, assess, prioritize, monitor and mitigate supplier, material, financial, operational, regulatory, geopolitical, quality and sustainability-related risks, while driving supplier compliance with applicable SEDEX requirements.

The position partners closely with Category Procurement, Business Units, Supply Chain, Operations, R&D, Finance, Legal, Food Safety & Quality and Sustainability teams to embed risk into category strategies, sourcing decisions and supplier relationship management. The role strengthens supply continuity, improves decision quality and supports uninterrupted delivery of the company strategic and growth objectives.

Job Description
Essential Functions & Responsibilities
1. Risk & Resilience Strategy and Operating Model
- Own and annually refresh the North America Procurement Risk & Resilience roadmap and three-year strategic plan, aligned with business priorities and ambitious risk-reduction targets.

- Define the procurement risk operating model, including risk appetite, governance routines, intake and prioritization, KPI tracking and leadership escalation pathways.

- Build capability roadmaps covering future-state tools, process improvements, automation opportunities and data enhancements.

- Continuously improve risk frameworks, methodologies and controls based on business needs, emerging threats and lessons learned.

2. Material, Supplier and Supply Continuity Risk
- Own the Material Risk Assessment methodology and annual AROP cycle, including methodology refresh, category engagement, risk scoring, mitigation planning and progress tracking.

- Identify and refine the variables used to measure risk so that the highest-priority materials, suppliers and exposures are targeted for mitigation.

- Lead third-party risk management across strategic and critical suppliers, monitoring financial, operational, quality, regulatory, ESG, geographic and geopolitical risks.

- Partner with category teams to develop and advance mitigation plans, including alternate sourcing, dual sourcing, contingency planning and other resilience solutions.

- Develop procurement resilience playbooks, conduct scenario planning and disruption simulations, and support crisis response and business recovery during supply disruptions.

- Maintain accurate material risk trackers and optimize their usability, data quality and relevance for decision-making and reporting.

3. Responsible sourcing
- Own North America Procurement’s SEDEX compliance program, governance and annual priorities, aligned with global requirements and business needs.

- Manage supplier registration, site association and required information in SEDEX, partnering with category teams and suppliers to address gaps and maintain accurate records.

- Monitor supplier and site compliance, track completion against established requirements and follow up on overdue or incomplete actions.

- Coordinate with Sustainability, category teams and suppliers on SEDEX related issues, escalations and remediation actions.

- Maintain SEDEX compliance dashboards and reporting, providing leadership with visibility to coverage, gaps, progress and priority actions.

- Develop guidance and training to support consistent SEDEX compliance across North America Procurement.

4. Risk Decision Support and Category Enablement
- Serve as the primary Procurement Risk point of contact for North America category teams and emerging risk issues, coordinating rapid assessment, stakeholder alignment and response recommendations.

- Build and maintain a catalog of tools, templates and risk profiles that enable category teams to incorporate risk into category strategies, sourcing strategies, supplier reviews, SRM activities and joint business plans.

- Lead regular category risk reviews, provide ad hoc guidance and troubleshooting, and drive mitigation progress against established KPIs.

- Assemble cross-functional teams and create situation-specific decision frameworks to prioritize and address complex or critical risk exposures.

5. Cross-Functional Governance and Business Partnership
- Lead governance routines with Supply Chain, Operations, Food Safety & Quality, R&D, Finance, Legal, Sustainability and other partners, integrating cross-functional risks that may affect supply continuity.

- Partner with Business Units to prioritize critical mitigation projects, align resources and ensure the risk agenda supports strategic business objectives.

- Present risk exposure, mitigation progress and priority decisions through BU performance routines and to senior Procurement and business leadership.

- Strengthen procurement governance controls, monitor remediation and corrective actions, ensure compliance with policies and regulatory requirements, and support internal and external audits.

6. Digital Risk Intelligence, Data and Reporting
- Lead the implementation and continuous improvement of procurement risk technologies, predictive analytics and automated monitoring capabilities.

- Integrate relevant internal and external intelligence sources into risk processes and decision-making.

- Build executive-ready dashboards and reporting that provide visibility to material and supplier risk exposure, mitigation pipelines, priority projects and performance against targets.

- Own country-of-origin mapping capability and governance, including data refresh cadence, data ownership, collection standards, system integration and cross-functional use cases.

7. Communication, Training and Adoption
- Develop and maintain annual stakeholder communication and engagement plans, including North America and Global Procurement risk updates.

- Maintain the Risk Hub on Proc Connect so current tools, templates, guidance and training materials are accessible and ready for use.

- Develop and deliver training on material and supplier risk, and maintain playbooks, SOPs and best-practice documentation to standardize processes and enable scalable adoption.

- Drive adoption of Procurement Risk tools, dashboards, templates and practices across North America Procurement and support future deployment of the methodology to other regions.

Required Qualifications
Education
- Bachelor’s degree in business, Supply Chain, Procurement, Sustainability, Engineering, Operational Excellence or a related field.

Experience
- 6-9 years of experience in Procurement, Supply Chain, Risk Management or a related business function.

- Demonstrated experience leading supplier or material risk programs and applying third-party risk management frameworks.

- Experience in CPG, food manufacturing or another regulated industry preferred.

- Experience implementing or managing risk technology platforms and analytics solutions.

Technical Skills
- Strong knowledge of supplier and material risk management, business continuity planning, SEDEX compliance, financial risk monitoring, regulatory compliance and crisis management.

- Strong analytical and problem-solving capability, with the ability to connect data, risk exposure and business impact.

- Proficiency with analytics and visualization tools; experience with Power BI, Tableau or similar platforms preferred.

- Understanding of AI-enabled monitoring, automation and emerging digital risk capabilities.

Leadership & Behavioral Competencies
- Acts as Procurement’s risk subject-matter expert and trusted advisor.

- Influences without authority and builds alignment across senior, cross-functional stakeholders.

- Communicates complex risk topics clearly and leads executive communications during disruptions.

- Demonstrates strong project management, organizational and stakeholder-management skills.

- Balances strategic thinking with disciplined operational execution.

- Brings curiosity, sound judgment, a continuous-improvement mindset and a willingness to challenge the status quo.
